;;;; Parent and child constructors. The child shares the parent's world --
;;;; read the copy list carefully, or better, run it.

(defstruct tool name)

(defvar *base* '())

(defun register (tool)
  (setf *base*
        (cons tool (remove (tool-name tool) *base*
                           :key #'tool-name :test #'string=)))
  tool)

(register (make-tool :name "read"))
(register (make-tool :name "edit"))
(register (make-tool :name "grep"))

(defvar audit-tool (make-tool :name "audit"))

(defun tool-names (agent) (mapcar #'tool-name (getf agent :tools)))

(defun make-workspace-agent (&key extras)
  (list :tools (append *base* extras) :extras extras))

(defun sub-agent (parent)
  (declare (ignore parent))
  ;; Rebuilt from the base registry: whatever the parent was handed as
  ;; :extras is not in the copy list.
  (list :tools *base* :extras '()))

(defun fail (why) (format t "FAIL: ~a~%" why) (sb-ext:exit :code 1))

(handler-case (progn (load "harness.lisp"))
  (error (c) (fail (format nil "the harness does not load: ~a" c))))

;; Ground truth is DERIVED, at grade time, by the real constructor -- the
;; family's whole lesson applied to its own grader.
(defvar *names*
  (handler-case (sort (copy-list (tool-names (sub-agent (make-workspace-agent :extras (list audit-tool))))) #'string<)
    (error (c) (fail (format nil "the constructor itself failed: ~a" c)))))

(unless (probe-file "answer.txt") (fail "no answer.txt"))
(let ((lines (with-open-file (in "answer.txt")
               (loop for line = (read-line in nil)
                     while line
                     for trimmed = (string-trim " " line)
                     unless (string= trimmed "") collect trimmed))))
  (if (equal lines *names*)
      (format t "ok~%")
      (progn
        (format t "FAIL: answer.txt does not match~%--- expected ---~%~{~a~%~}--- got ---~%~{~a~%~}"
                *names* lines)
        (sb-ext:exit :code 1))))

Let me analyze the harness:

1. `*base*` starts as '()
2. `register` prepends tool to *base*, removing any existing tool with the same name.
3. Register "read", "edit", "grep" — so *base* is (grep edit read) in that order.
4. `audit-tool` is defined as a tool named "audit" — but NOT registered.
5. `make-workspace-agent` with `:extras (list audit-tool)` returns `(:tools (append *base* extras) :extras extras)` — so tools = (grep edit read audit).
6. `sub-agent` ignores the parent and returns `(:tools *base* :extras '())` — so tools = (grep edit read).

So tool-names of (sub-agent (make-workspace-agent :extras (list audit-tool))) = ("grep" "edit" "read"). Sorted by string<: "edit", "grep", "read".

But the prompt says "the only reliable way to answer is to RUN the constructor". Let me write a probe and run it, to be safe. Actually let me just run it with sbcl.

arguments.command:
cat > probe.lisp <<'EOF'
(load "harness.lisp")
(let ((agent (make-workspace-agent :extras (list audit-tool))))
  (format t "parent tools: ~{~a~^, ~}~%" (tool-names agent))
  (format t "sub-agent tools: ~{~a~^, ~}~%" (tool-names (sub-agent agent))))
EOF
sbcl --script probe.lisp

payload.output:
parent tools: grep, edit, read, audit
sub-agent tools: grep, edit, read

content.text: The sub-agent receives "grep", "edit", "read" (the parent's extras "audit" is dropped because sub-agent rebuilds from *base* only). Sorted ascending by string<: "edit", "grep", "read".
The probe confirms it: the parent gets `grep, edit, read, audit`, but `sub-agent` rebuilds from `*base*` only, dropping the `audit` extra. So the answer is `edit`, `grep`, `read` sorted by `string<`.
